directive in CSS.\n\n### Official Plugins (Tailwind Labs)\n\n#### Typography Plugin - Style Markdown/CMS Content\n\nWhen to use: Displaying blog posts, documentation, or any HTML from Markdown/CMS.\n\nInstallation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm add -D @tailwindcss/typography\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nConfiguration (v4 syntax):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;css\n/* src/index.css */\n@import \"tailwindcss\";\n@plugin \"@tailwindcss/typography\";\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUsage:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;html\n\u003carticle class=\"prose lg:prose-xl dark:prose-invert\"\u003e\n  {{ markdown_content }}\n\u003c/article\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAvailable classes:\n\n- &#96;prose&#96;- Base typography styles\n- &#96;prose-sm&#96;,&#96;prose-base&#96;,&#96;prose-lg&#96;,&#96;prose-xl&#96;,&#96;prose-2xl&#96;- Size variants\n- &#96;dark:prose-invert&#96;- Dark mode styles\n\n---\n\n#### Forms Plugin - Reset Form Element Styles\n\nWhen to use: Building custom forms without shadcn/ui components, or need consistent cross-browser form styling.\n\nInstallation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm add -D @tailwindcss/forms\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nConfiguration (v4 syntax):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;css\n/* src/index.css */\n@import \"tailwindcss\";\n@plugin \"@tailwindcss/forms\";\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWhat it does:\n\n- Resets browser default form styles\n- Makes form elements styleable with Tailwind utilities\n- Fixes cross-browser inconsistencies for inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios\n\nNote: Less critical for shadcn/ui users (they have pre-styled form components), but still useful for basic forms.\n\n---\n\n### Common Plugin Errors\n\nThese errors happen when using v3 syntax in v4 projects:\n\n❌ WRONG (v3 config file syntax):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// tailwind.config.js\nmodule.exports = {\n  plugins: [require('@tailwindcss/typography')]\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n❌ WRONG (@import instead of @plugin):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;css\n@import \"@tailwindcss/typography\"; [postgres-drizzle by ccheney/robust-skills](https://skills.sh/ccheney/robust-skills/postgres-drizzle)\n\n# Drizzle ORM on skills.sh\n\nDrizzle ORM is a modern TypeScript-first ORM with zero dependencies, compile-time type safety, and SQL-like syntax, optimized for edge runtimes and serverless environments.[1]\n\n## Installation \u0026 Setup\n\nInstall the core package and a database driver:[1]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install drizzle-orm\nnpm install pg            # PostgreSQL\nnpm install mysql2        # MySQL\nnpm install better-sqlite3 # SQLite\nnpm install -D drizzle-kit # For migrations\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Basic Usage\n\nDefine a schema, create a database client, then use the query builder API:[1]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { pgTable, serial, text, timestamp } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';\nexport const users = pgTable('users', {\n  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),\n  email: text('email').notNull().unique(),\n  name: text('name').notNull(),\n  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow(),\n});\n\n// Query examples\nawait db.insert(users).values({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' });\nconst allUsers = await db.select().from(users);\nawait db.update(users).set({ name: 'Jane' }).where(eq(users.id, 1));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Database-Specific Skills\n\n**Cloudflare D1**: Use &#96;db.batch()&#96; for transactions instead of SQL BEGIN/COMMIT, test migrations locally first, and use &#96;integer&#96; with &#96;mode: 'timestamp'&#96; for dates.[2]\n\n**PostgreSQL**: Always index foreign keys, use the relational queries API to avoid N+1 queries, and enable connection pooling in production.[5]\n\n## Key Tools\n\n- &#96;drizzle-kit generate&#96; - Generate SQL migrations from schema changes[1]\n- &#96;drizzle-kit studio&#96; - Visual database browser[2]\n- &#96;drizzle-kit push&#96; - Push schema directly (dev only)[5]",

Static (Auto-Prerendered)\n\nSynchronous code, imports, pure computations - prerendered at build time:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport default function Page() {\n  return (\n    \u003cheader\u003e\n      \u003ch1\u003eOur Blog\u003c/h1\u003e  {/* Static - instant */}\n      \u003cnav\u003e...\u003c/nav\u003e\n    \u003c/header\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Cached (use cache)\n\nAsync data that doesn't need fresh fetches every request:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nasync function BlogPosts() {\n  'use cache'\n  cacheLife('hours')\n\n  const posts = await db.posts.findMany()\n  return \u003cPostList posts={posts} /\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. streams in */}\n      \u003c/Suspense\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  )\n}\n\nasync function UserPreferences() {\n  const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme')?.value\n  return \u003cp\u003eTheme: {theme}\u003c/p\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## use cache Directive\n\n### File Level\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use cache'\n\nexport default async function Page() {\n  // Entire page is cached\n  const data = await fetchData()\n  return \u003cdiv\u003e{data}\u003c/div\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Component Level\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport async function CachedComponent() {\n  'use cache'\n  const data = await fetchData()\n  return \u003cdiv\u003e{data}\u003c/div\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Function Level\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport async function getData() {\n  'use cache'\n  return db.query('SELECT * FROM posts')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Cache Profiles\n\n### Built-in Profiles\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use cache'                    // Default: 5m stale, 15m revalidate\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use cache: remote'           // Platform-provided cache (Redis, KV)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use cache: private'          // For compliance, allows runtime APIs\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### cacheLife() - Custom Lifetime\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'\n\nasync function getData() {\n  'use cache'\n  cacheLife('hours')  // Built-in profile\n  return fetch('/api/data')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBuilt-in profiles:&#96;'default'&#96;,&#96;'minutes'&#96;,&#96;'hours'&#96;,&#96;'days'&#96;,&#96;'weeks'&#96;,&#96;'max'&#96;\n\n### Inline Configuration\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nasync function getData() {\n  'use cache'\n  cacheLife({\n    stale: 3600,      // 1 hour - serve stale while revalidating\n    revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours - background revalidation interval\n    expire: 86400,    // 1 day - hard expiration\n  })\n  return fetch('/api/data')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Cache Invalidation\n\n### cacheTag() - ### 2. `playwright-skill` -- No, `playwright-best-practices` does NOT cover the same thing

Your current skill is a **browser automation runner** -- it auto-detects dev servers, writes scripts to `/tmp`, executes them with a visible browser, and provides helper functions (`safeClick`, `safeType`, `detectDevServers`). It's a hands-on tool for running ad-hoc automation tasks.

`playwright-best-practices` is a **reference guide** for how to write good Playwright tests (50+ patterns, POM vs fixtures architecture, decision trees). It doesn't run anything or auto-detect servers.

These complement each other but don't replace each other. **Your current skill is unique in its approach. The `playwright-cli` from Microsoft (which you chose to install) is the closer replacement for browser automation.**

---

### 3. `seo` -- Yes, the alternative covers the same thing (with different emphasis)

| Aspect | Your current skill | `seo-audit` (coreyhaines31) |
|---|---|---|
| Technical SEO (robots, canonical, sitemap) | Yes (with code examples) | Yes (with audit checklists) |
| On-page (titles, meta, headings, images) | Yes | Yes |
| Internal linking | Yes | Yes |
| Mobile SEO | Yes | Yes |
| Structured data (JSON-LD) | **Yes, full code examples** | Mentioned, but warns about detection limitations |
| International SEO (hreflang) | Yes | Not covered |
| Content quality / E-E-A-T | No | **Yes** |
| Site-type guidance (SaaS, e-commerce) | No | **Yes** |
| Audit reporting structure | Basic checklist | **Full prioritized action plan format** |
| Keyword targeting | No | **Yes** |

The alternative is broader (adds E-E-A-T, keyword targeting, site-type guidance) but your current one has more JSON-LD code examples and hreflang coverage. Overall, `seo-audit` is a superset for most use cases. **Recommended: replace.**

Here is a concise explanation.

## What `accessibility` and `playwright-skill` were

Under `.cursor/skills/`, almost everything is a **symbolic link** to a folder under `.agents/skills/<name>`. So:

- `.cursor/skills/accessibility` → `../../.agents/skills/accessibility`
- `.cursor/skills/playwright-skill` → `../../.agents/skills/playwright-skill`

Those names matched the **old** skills you later replaced with `accessibility-compliance`, `playwright-best-practices`, and `playwright-cli`. The real folders under `.agents/skills/` were removed, so those two links became **dangling** (pointing at paths that no longer exist).

**Exception:** `agents-md-sync` is a **real directory** in `.cursor/skills/` (project-specific skill), not a symlink to `.agents/skills/`.

## Why many skills are “not” in `.cursor/`

They are not duplicated; the setup is **one canonical copy** + **shortcuts**:

| Location | Role |
|----------|------|
| **`.agents/skills/`** | Where `pnpm dlx skills add …` installs skill content (the “source of truth” on disk). |
| **`.cursor/skills/`** | Cursor’s usual place for skills the IDE can attach. Here, most entries are **symlinks** into `.agents/skills/` so you don’t maintain two copies. |

So skills “not in `.cursor/`” usually mean either:

1. They were **never symlinked** after install (e.g. after adding new skills), or  
2. You’re looking only at `.cursor/` and the files live under `.agents/skills/` via those links.

**What I changed locally:** I removed the broken `accessibility` and `playwright-skill` links and added symlinks for the new skills: `accessibility-compliance`, `drizzle-orm`, `playwright-best-practices`, `playwright-cli`, and `seo-audit`. Now `.cursor/skills/` should line up with your current `.agents/skills/` set (plus `agents-md-sync` as a normal folder).

If anything still looks wrong in the IDE, restart Cursor or re-open the folder so it picks up the updated symlinks.
